summary: Provides forward-only raw-I/O adapters used for default sequential remote reads and for gzip decoding. ForwardOnlyReader wraps a sized read callable and a close callable, owns closure, and optionally maps native exceptions to package errors on read and close. IterBytesReader adapts a byte-chunk iterator, holding at most one pending chunk as a memoryview without draining the iterator.
key_classes: ForwardOnlyReader(read, close, map_error=None) — non-seekable RawIOBase over a sized read callable; translates errors via map_error at read and close time
IterBytesReader(chunks, close, map_error=None) — ForwardOnlyReader over an iterator of byte chunks retaining at most one chunk
extension_points: Backends produce sequential streams by wrapping their native body in io.BufferedReader(ForwardOnlyReader(...)) or IterBytesReader(...) and passing a map_error callable that returns a package exception (or None to leave the native error)
lifecycle_notes: The reader owns the close callable: close() invokes it once and marks the handle closed even if it raises
Error translation is deferred to consumption and close, matching the documented sequential error timing
documentation_hooks: Backend author guide: producing sequential streams and error mapping
docs/read-access-modes.md sequential row: remote handles are forward-only
risks: readable() does not check closed state while readinto does, unlike RangedReader, which checks on every method
A map_error callable that itself raises replaces the original exception

evidence.detail: S3 sequential reads wrap ForwardOnlyReader in BufferedReader
HTTP sequential reads use IterBytesReader with _map_error
